fact: Sudan's Judicial Authority said on 12 March 2016 it would start implementing an e-portal and court computerisation project from the following Monday, first phase costed at USD 600,000, with a Supreme Court case-flow system and later extension to all civil and criminal courts.

Intelligent CIO reports that Al Taqnyah Business Solutions was chosen for the automation of the Sudan Judiciary, that its Technical Manager says phase one is finished and phase two, covering automation of the whole judiciary system, is about to start.
